questions.q: List the four primary hardware components of a computer system as per the von Neumann architecture.
questions.a: The four primary hardware components are: (1) Central Processing Unit (CPU), (2) Primary Memory (RAM/ROM), (3) Input Devices, and (4) Output Devices. Secondary storage is often considered a fifth essential component in modern systems. A wrong answer that omits the CPU or memory, or includes software like "Windows", reveals that the student has not internalised the hardware-only perspective of the von Neumann model and is conflating physical components with logical layers.

questions.q: Explain in your own words why a computer with only hardware components (CPU, memory, keyboard, monitor) but no software cannot perform any useful task for a user.
questions.a: Hardware provides the physical capability to compute, but without software (instructions), the CPU has no program to fetch, decode, or execute. The hardware remains an inert collection of circuits. A wrong answer that says "the computer will still work but slowly" or "the user can type commands directly into the CPU" shows a fundamental misunderstanding of the stored-program concept: the CPU only understands machine code, not human intent, and that machine code must be supplied as software.

questions.q: Classify each of the following as Hardware (H) or Software (S), and if Software, further classify as System Software (SS), Application Software (AS), or Programming Tool (PT): (a) Linux Ubuntu, (b) Laser Printer, (c) Python Interpreter, (d) SSD, (e) Tally ERP 9, (f) Device Driver for Wi-Fi card.
questions.a: (a) Linux Ubuntu – SS (Operating System); (b) Laser Printer – H (Output Device); (c) Python Interpreter – PT (translates high-level code to machine code); (d) SSD – H (Secondary Storage); (e) Tally ERP 9 – AS (Customised accounting software); (f) Device Driver – SS (manages specific hardware). A wrong classification of the Python Interpreter as Application Software indicates the student does not distinguish between tools that create software and software that solves end-user problems. Misclassifying a device driver as application software shows confusion about the system software layer.

questions.q: Compare RAM and ROM across three dimensions: volatility, write-access during normal operation, and typical content stored. Present your answer as a 2×3 table.
questions.a:
| Dimension | RAM | ROM |
|-----------|-----|-----|
| Volatility | Volatile (loses data on power-off) | Non-volatile (retains data without power) |
| Write-access | Read-write (user programs modify it constantly) | Read-only in normal operation (written only during manufacturing or firmware updates) |
| Typical content | Currently running programs, OS kernel, active data | Bootloader (BIOS/UEFI), firmware, permanent microcode |

A wrong answer that claims ROM is "read-only forever" ignores modern EEPROM/flash updates. Claiming RAM stores the OS permanently confuses primary memory with secondary storage.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "A smartphone is not a computer system because it does not have a separate CPU, keyboard, and monitor." Provide a reasoned judgment using the definition of a computer system.
questions.a: The statement is false. A smartphone integrates all von Neumann components: a System-on-Chip (SoC) contains CPU, GPU, and memory controllers (processing); built-in RAM and flash storage (primary/secondary memory); touchscreen (combined input/output); and runs an OS (Android/iOS) with apps. The form factor differs, but the architectural components are present. A wrong answer that agrees with the statement reveals a rigid, desktop-centric mental model and failure to apply the abstract definition to a concrete, modern device.

questions.q: Design a block diagram for a computer system used in an ATM (Automated Teller Machine). Label all hardware components (including specialised I/O devices) and indicate the flow of data when a user withdraws cash. Briefly describe the role of the OS and the banking application software in this flow.
questions.a: A good answer includes: CPU (SoC), RAM, Secure Cryptoprocessor (hardware security module), Card Reader (input), Keypad (input), Display (output), Receipt Printer (output), Cash Dispenser (output), Network Interface (communication), Encrypted Storage (secondary). Data flow: Card Reader → CPU (verify PIN via OS & banking app) → Network → Bank Server → Response → CPU → Cash Dispenser + Printer + Display. OS manages hardware resources, schedules tasks, handles secure storage; banking app implements withdrawal logic, communicates with bank server. A poor diagram omits the secure element, network interface, or treats the cash dispenser as a generic printer, showing inability to map abstract components to a specialised embedded system.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A computer system is an integrated set of physical components (hardware) and ______ sets (software) that work together to accept input, process data, store information, and produce output.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are buying a new ______ for your Class 11 projects.
Fill in the blank: Group the code items (Windows ______, MS Office) as software.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to (1) correctly classify any given computer component as hardware or software and further categorise hardware into input, output, processing, memory, or storage, and software into system, application, or programming tools; (2) explain the functional interdependence between hardware and software using the concept.
